description:
5/22/2024  – at around 11:07 a.m. at the intersection of SE Oak Street and SE 6th Avenue.
 
This crash was vehicle versus pedestrian with the pedestrian having minor injuries (minor scrapes).  
 Weather was cl ear; pavement surface was dry . 
 The driver said that they pulled up to the intersection going north on SE 6th Avenue with intent to turn right to go east on SE Oak Street. They were looking to their left as SE Oak Street is a one -way street. When traffic 
cleared , they began to pull out onto SE Oak Street. They did not see that the pedestrian walking on the sidewalk 
from their right. As they started to pull out, they bumped the pedestrian with their vehicle and knocked them 
down. The driver immediately backed up, got out, and helped the pedestrian. A witness to the crash provided 
the exact same details.  
 
The pedestrian said the driver was not guilty of anything and believed it was just an accident.  
No citations were issued . 
 
Staff did not visit location.

6/1/2024 – at around 6:44 p.m. at the intersection of NW 185th Avenue and NE Holly Street.
 
This crash involved two vehicles where one vehicle rearended the other. A driver and passenger were 
transported to area hospitals with complaint of injuries.  
 Weather was cloudy , pavement surface was dry . 
 
According to re porting officer, the young driver was driving south on 185
th and struck the rear of the second 
vehicle as it was stopped at the intersection. The other driver was not interviewed.  
 
A witness said they were driving northbound on 185th Ave approaching the redlight at Holly St when they say the 
vehicle rearend the other. They said the 2nd vehicle did not seem to slow down and struck the vehicle.  
 Unknown if citations were issued.  
 
Staff did not visit crash location.

6/4/2024 – at around 8:13 a.m. at  the intersection of SE 12th Avenue and SE Walnut Street.
 
 This crash was vehicle versus scooter  with the scooter operator having suspected serious  injuries .  
 Weather was cloudy , pavement surface was dry . 
 The driver said they were travelling south on SE 12th Avenue and came to a stop at the stop sign. They 
proceeded through the intersection when the person on the scooter who traveling west on SE 12th Avenue did 
not stop for the stop sign. The driver said they struck the scooter before they could react to the scooter . 
 
The scooter operator said they were going west on SE 12th Avenue and stopped for the stop sign then 
proceeded through the intersection. He said he guessed he just did not see the silver vehicle and suddenly there 
it was. He said the vehicle struck him and he fell to the pavement.  
 
There were no independent witnesses who observed crash.   
 No citations were issued.  
 Staff did not visit crash location.

6/5/2024 – at around 8:07 a.m. at approximately 175 ft north of the intersection of SE Brookwood Avenue and SE TV Highway.  
 
This crash was a vehicle versus motorcycle with the motorcyclist having suspected serious injuries.  
  
 Weather was clear, pavement surface was dry.  
 
The driver said they made a right turn  out from the gas station parking lot onto SE Brookwood Ave. The driver 
said they turned to  change lanes to the left turn lane to go onto SE 49th Ave and hit the motorcycle. The driver 
said they checked their mirror but didn't see the motorcycle.  
 
The motorcyclist said they were  riding northbound on SE Brookwood Ave. They had switched lanes just past the 
intersection of SE Tualatin Valley Highway. The motorcyclist said they were going about 35 miles per hour after 
they switched lanes, they saw a car coming out from the driveway at the gas station and made an aggressive move, cutting vehicles off. The motorcyclist was unable to maneuver out of the way before the vehicle collided with them.  
 A witness stated they were traveling n orthbound on SE Brookwood Ave. They continued through the 
intersection at TV Hwy and SE Brookwood Ave. They saw the two lanes on SE Brookwood Ave merged in to one 
lane after the intersection. The witness saw the motorcycle, traveling next to them in the same direction, speed 
up to move ahead of them before the two lanes merged. The motorcycle sped up and got in front of the witness. There was a 76 -gas station on the right -side corner after the intersection. The witness saw a vehicle, 
pull out of the 76 -gas station to head n orthbound on SE Brookwood Ave. The witness saw the vehicle drive 
across two lanes of traffic to get into the left -hand turn lane, turning onto SE 49TH Ave. This is when they saw 
the vehicle and motorcycle collide.  
 The driver was cited for an unsafe lane change and failure to yield right of way.  
 Staff did not visit the crash site.

6/5/2024 – at around 11:07 p.m. at approximately 25 ft west of the intersection of NE Arrington Road and NE Cornell Road.
 
 This crash was a vehicle versus motorcycle with the motorcyclist having suspected serious injuries.  
 Weather was clear, pavement surface was dry.  
 An officer on duty working patrol in uniform at the intersection of NE 25th Avenue / NE Cornell Rd. when they observed a red motorcycle without any license plates attached to it. The officer positioned themselves behind 
the motorcycle as the driver turned into the lane to travel westbound on NE Cornell Rd from NE 25th avenue. 
The officer activated their overhead emergency patrol vehicle lights and initiated a traffic stop on the driver of the motorcycle. The motorcyclist immediately sped off westbound on NE  Cornell Rd. at an extremely high rate of 
speed which was estimated to be 60+ MPH using the patrol vehicles speedometer which showed the officer going approx. 25 MPH.  The officer notified dispatch of the direction of travel and the description of the  
motorcyclist, that they had eluded the officer, they were no longer in pursuit and had shut off their  emergency 
lights. As the officer continued to drive westbound on NE Cornell Rd. and approached NE 17th Avenue, they 
observed numerous people around a red motorcycle which was down on the ground at the intersection of NE Arrington Rd. / NE Cornell Rd. This is when the officer realized this was the same driver and motorcycle which had just eluded them. The officer requested additional officers and medical assistance.  
 The motorcyclist was not interviewed and was transported due to their injuries.  
 The motorcyclist was arrested.    
  
Staff did not visit the crash site.

6/9/2024 – at around 6:06 p.m. at approximately 15 ft north of the intersection of SE 10th Avenue and SE Oak Street.

 This crash was single vehicle motorcycle crash with the motorcyclist having suspected serious injuries.  
 Weather was clear, pavement surface was dry.  
 
The motorcyclist said that they were in the southbound lane of SE 10
th Avenue stopped a t the red light. They 
were struck from behind hard enough that the motorcyclist was thrown over their handlebars and  sustained a 
deep laceration to their left shin. The motorcyclist was transported . 
 
A witness  said they had been sitting at the red light when they heard the crash. They looked over and saw the 
motorcyclist lying  on the roadway in front of their motorcycle, which was down on its side. The witness stated 
the car had been driven by a Hispanic male, and the passenger had been a Hispanic female which had left the 
scene south on 10th.   The vehicle was located nearby along with the driver and passenger. The driver  did not speak English however 
the officer was able to converse via Google Translate, and with help from the passenger. The driver claimed that he had not impacted the motorcycle and that the rider had merely fallen over. When confronted with that their 
front license plate, which  had been found at the scene of the crash, the driver claimed it had been loose, and 
had just fallen off.  The passenger refused to be interviewed.  
 The driver was cited for  Unlicensed Driver, Driving Without Insurance, and Careless Driving.
